title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-06
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard transfer captures a scorching June ’70 Fillmore West set, highlighted by the Alligator jam, rare New Orleans, and a blistering Dancing Jam.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD transfer delivers clear, well‑balanced audio that lets the band’s chemistry shine—especially the interplay between Jerry and Bob after the Alligator drums.  The show is a second‑set monster with an hour‑long jam sequence (Alligator → Darkness Darkness → Lovelight > Not Fade Away > Lovelight) plus standout moments like the rare New Orleans, the fiery Dancing Jam and an unforgettable Attics of My Life.  A few minor mix hiccups appear on the Uncle John’s Band encore, but they don’t detract from the overall brilliance.

ai_rating.rationale: Over a dozen enthusiastic reviews (mostly 4‑5 stars) praise both performance and sound quality; only occasional minor complaints about mix or encore keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear, well‑balanced SBD transfer (Charlie Miller) with good instrument separation; not as crisp as some legendary dates (5/15/70) but far superior to many other 1970 releases. Minor mix issue: Jerry’s guitar drops out briefly on the Uncle John’s Band outro.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is only partially present but solid; the second set erupts after Alligator into an hour‑long improvisational suite that builds through Darkness Darkness, Lovelight sequences and a scorching jam climax. The flow is tight, energetic, and showcases the band’s peak summer ’70 form.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his soaring lead on the Alligator jam, tight interplay with Bob after drums, and overall guitar brilliance (aside from a brief drop‑out on UJB).
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for vocal strength on Attics of My Life and strong rhythmic partnership with Jerry during post‑Alligator jams.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming highlighted as “locked in” and a driving force throughout the long jam sequence; occasional off‑beat feel mentioned only on the UJB outro.
